title: Sandy Beaches in Novigrad, Croatia: Honest Guide 2027
metaDescription: Novigrad, Istria has no true sandy beach. Here is which beaches are fine pebble, rock or concrete, and where the nearest real sand is, with drive times.
content:
## Is there a sandy beach in Novigrad?

No. Novigrad's coast is pebble, rock slabs and concrete sunbathing platforms, in line with most of Istria and Croatia. Some stretches have fine gravel, but nothing that counts as sand. Travelers who need sand for toddlers or sandcastles must drive out of town: Kanegra (fine gravel) is about 30 minutes away and Bijeca in Medulin (real sand) about 1 hour 15 minutes.

## Beach surfaces in Novigrad, one by one

### Karpinjan: pebble, shaded promenade
Karpinjan starts roughly 300 m north of the marina and is reached on foot from the old town in about 10 minutes. The surface is pebble with some paved sections. A long promenade and a belt of trees give partial shade, which is better than at most Istrian town beaches. The sea deepens at a moderate pace, so it works for school-age children but small toddlers need close watching at the edge. Crowds peak in July and August. Parking is limited near the marina, so walking or cycling is easier.

### Mareda: concrete and rock, Blue Flag water
Mareda lies about 4 km south of the centre, next to the Aminess Maravea campsite area. The main section is concrete platforms and rock slabs with showers and changing cabins, and the water is clear and holds Blue Flag status. Entry is by ladder or rocky steps rather than a sandy slope, and the shallows are uneven. Shade is thin on the platforms. Parking is available nearby, and it fills by late morning in peak season. The quieter stretch beyond the landscaped part is bare stone slabs and suits adults better than small children. Wear water shoes.

### Pineta and Kastanija: pebble and rock under pines
South of town, Pineta and Kastanija have pebble and rock entries with pine trees behind them, so shade is easy to find. They are good for snorkelling and less crowded than the town beaches. They are not good for toddlers because the rock and stones make walking into the water awkward.

### Štrunac and Dajla: wild pebble coves
North of Novigrad, the Dajla coast has long rocky and pebble sections with almost no infrastructure. Štrunac is a pebble cove with no facilities, so bring water, shade and food. Parking is informal and close to the shore. It is quiet even in August, which is its main advantage.

### Maestral, Laguna and Sirena: hotel-area beaches
The beaches in front of the Aminess Maestral and Laguna Novigrad hotels are a mix of pebble and concrete, and Maestral has held Blue Flag status. Their value is easy access and facilities, not softness underfoot.

## Nearest beaches with softer surfaces

### Kanegra, Savudrija: fine gravel, 25 km
Kanegra is the nearest cove with a genuinely gentle entry. It is a short beach of fine gravel, around 75 m long, in a bay with trees that provide plenty of shade. The water is shallow at the edge, so it suits young children well. The car park is about 500 m from the sand, so carry gear light. It is a short beach and fills quickly on summer weekends, so arrive before 10:00. It is close to the Slovenian border, and the naturist area is separate and signed. The drive from Novigrad takes about 30 minutes.

### Bijeca, Medulin: the real sandy option, about 90 km
Bijeca is the sandy beach that Istria's families head to. The sand is soft, the water stays shallow far from the shore, and it suits toddlers and non-swimmers. Shade is limited, so bring an umbrella. It is crowded from late June to August, and parking is paid in season. From Novigrad it takes roughly 1 hour 15 minutes by car via the Istrian Y motorway, so plan a full day, not a quick swim.

## Practical tips for sand-seekers

- Pack water shoes for every Novigrad beach except Kanegra. Rock and stones are the norm.
- For children under five, fine gravel at Kanegra is the compromise. Real sand means Medulin.
- Go to Kanegra early. By 10:30 on a July weekend, the car park and beach are busy.
- Bring your own umbrella for the rocky coves and Bijeca. Natural shade there is scarce.
- Water quality is not the problem in Novigrad. The sea is clear and clean, which is why pebble and rock beaches here still work for swimming and snorkelling.

## Verdict: does Novigrad suit people who want sand?

No. Novigrad works for clear water, shade and a walkable old town, not for sand. If sand is the priority, this base is a poor choice because the nearest true sand is a 90 km drive away. A day trip to Bijeca is a long haul for a family with young children, and it is not worth doing more than once. Kanegra is the realistic compromise for gentle entry and shade. Choose Novigrad if you can accept pebble and concrete. Base yourself in the Medulin area instead if sand matters more than anything else.

## FAQ

See the questions below for quick answers.

faq.question: Does Novigrad have a sandy beach?
faq.answer: No. Novigrad's beaches are pebble, rock and concrete. A few have fine gravel, but none has natural sand.

faq.question: Where is the nearest sandy beach to Novigrad?
faq.answer: Bijeca in Medulin is the nearest true sandy beach, about 90 km south and roughly 1 hour 15 minutes by car. Kanegra near Savudrija, about 30 minutes north, has fine gravel rather than sand.

faq.question: Which Novigrad beach is best for small children?
faq.answer: Karpinjan is the easiest in town, with pebble, partial shade and walking access. For a gentler, shallower entry, Kanegra is the better choice, though it is a 30-minute drive.

faq.question: Are Novigrad beaches rocky?
faq.answer: Many are. Mareda is mostly concrete platforms and rock slabs, and Pineta, Kastanija and the Dajla coast are pebble and rock. Water shoes are recommended.

faq.question: Do I need to pay to enter beaches in Novigrad?
faq.answer: Entry to the public beaches is free. You pay for sunbeds, umbrellas and parking where it is charged, such as at Bijeca in season.

faq.question: Is the sea in Novigrad clean enough for swimming?
faq.answer: Yes. The water is clear, and Mareda and Maestral are Blue Flag beaches. The limitation is the surface, not the quality.

quickAnswer: Novigrad has no natural sandy beach. Its beaches are pebble, rock and concrete, with some fine gravel. The nearest fine-gravel cove is Kanegra, about 25 km north (30 minutes). The nearest true sand is Bijeca in Medulin, roughly 90 km south (about 1 hour 15 minutes by car).
